name: Flashcard (Self-Assessed Recall)
summary: Card shows prompt on front. User attempts recall, flips to check. Self-sorts into 'Know' / 'Still Learning.'

aiGenerability.notes: Direct fact-to-card conversion. AI excels at generating front/back pairs from any knowledge base, including multilingual (translation pairs) and visual (definition → image).

front.description: The prompt or question shown on the front of the card.

back.description: Structured content for the back of the card.

title.description: The key concept or answer being recalled. Displayed prominently as the heading of the back side. This is the thing the learner is trying to retrieve — e.g. 'Photosynthesis', 'Brasília', '1912'.

detail.description: A concise explanation or definition that reinforces the title. Displayed below the title in smaller text. 1-2 sentences max. e.g. 'The process by which plants convert light energy, water, and CO₂ into glucose and oxygen.'

category.description: A short label shown as a tag or chip on the back. Groups the card thematically. e.g. 'Biology', 'Geography', 'Ancient Egypt'. Helps learners build mental models across cards.

hint.description: Optional hint displayed before flipping, for scaffolding.

topic.description: The lesson topic this card belongs to. Used for deck organization and displayed as context in the card UI. e.g. 'Ancient Egypt', 'The Solar System'.

difficulty.description: Difficulty level based on recall distance.

tags.description: Tags for filtering and organizing cards.

ux.animation: card-flip 3D rotation with easing, swipe-left/right for navigation
ux.mobileNotes: Full-screen card centered. Tap to flip or swipe to advance. Support one-handed use. Show progress (N/M cards). Soft edge-to-edge design on small screens.

ageAdaptations.8-10: Larger cards (90% viewport width) with bigger text (18-20pt front, 16pt back). Simplified language. Large hint text. No time pressure. Swipe-based navigation is optional; tap-to-flip primary. Emoji or icons on cards for visual interest.
ageAdaptations.11-13: Standard card layout. Swipe to navigate. Optional timer for speed mode. Longer, more complex definitions allowed. Progress counter visible (e.g., '7 / 20'). Hint optional.
ageAdaptations.14-16: Speed mode with timer (10-30s per card). Swipe-only navigation with velocity-based interactions. Option to mark card for review without flipping. Spaced repetition algorithm (show hard cards more often). Keyboard support on desktop (arrow keys, space to flip).
